business_problem: Edenred needed to replace fragmented country-specific payment stacks with one global super app that could keep data consistent and responsive during the extreme lunch-rush transaction spike.
solution_summary: Edenred built Edenred+ on MongoDB Atlas to unify digital payment services that had previously been split across country-specific legacy stacks. The new platform uses a microservices architecture anchored by two repositories: a point-of-sale repository for highly variable merchant and location data, and a transaction repository for real-time payment authorizations and balance updates. Atlas's document model lets Edenred preserve one logical database while adapting merchant data to local market differences, and its geospatial capabilities power the app's store finder. On the transaction side, Atlas processes out-of-order events while maintaining accurate balances during lunch-rush peaks. The team paired that with smart indexing, data-retention automation, and Atlas's multi-cloud flexibility, even moving specific clusters to AWS and Google Cloud through the Atlas interface when I/O limits emerged with another provider.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the global payment platform's database layer for merchant discovery, transaction processing, indexing, and multi-cloud operations.

data_flow: Merchant and geolocation data flows into Atlas-backed point-of-sale documents for store discovery, while payment authorizations flow through the transaction repository in real time; indexed Atlas clusters keep balances accurate during lunch-rush spikes and enrich completed transactions with recognizable merchant details.
business_outcome: Edenred can scale a globally reusable payment super app, keep transactions accurate under lunch-rush load, and deliver richer merchant discovery and recommendation experiences across multiple markets.
metrics: Operating in 45 countries and processing around EUR30 billion annually in restaurant spending alone.
The company connects more than 60 million users with a network of over 2 million merchants.
The lunch rush is a concentrated spike between 12:00pm and 2:00pm when millions of users transact simultaneously.
The platform is engineered to handle up to 15 million MongoDB transactions during the intense two-hour lunch window.
Already serving more than one million users, with a clear path to six million by 2026.
MongoDB Atlas now powers operations in France, Poland, Bulgaria, and Mexico.
architecture_clues: Edenred split the architecture into dedicated transaction and point-of-sale repositories.
Out-of-order transactions are reconciled to preserve correct balances.
Specific Atlas clusters can be moved between cloud providers through the Atlas interface.
evidence_quotes: MongoDB allows us to maintain a single database that adapts to the data available in each market.
If a user's balance is wrong during lunch, that's an immediate failure of service.
With MongoDB, we now have real-time data availability that allows us to enrich transactions instantly and deploy robust features globally.
